headings.title: Center actions and bounded deep links

html:
Notification publication and observation

Notification Center presents records owned by the existing event store. Producing an inbox item, publishing a UI invalidation, displaying a browser alert and marking an item read are separate operations. None of those operations establishes that a source task or external effect succeeded. The user guide explains controls, delivery and history limits.

flowchart LR P[Reminder, task, monitor or product tool] --> S[EventStore notification record] S --> H[Controller hub and recovery checkpoint] S --> U[Shared UI invalidation broker] U --> B[Open browser observer] B -->|Fetch current history| A[Notification routes and public projection] A -->|Read canonical records| S A --> B B --> D[History and optional alert] B -->|Explicit read or dismiss action| A

Storage and publication

Event models separate notification status from event and run status. Creation accepts a title of up to 160 characters, a nonempty message of up to 24,000 characters, source/event/run/request identities, severity and metadata. The event-store factory selects RAM storage for registered Controller paths; standalone consumers retain the SQLite implementation. The hub's publication and disk checkpoint boundaries are described in State.

Creation normalizes the title, preserves message line breaks within its bound, sets timestamps and inserts unread items when notifications are enabled. A disabled preference instead creates a read item with notifications_suppressed metadata. The preference provider defaults to enabled if absent or if it raises. Saving the UI preference as disabled also marks existing unread items read through the settings route owner.

Callers can request deduplication by source type and nonempty source ID. Existing read or dismissed records still count as prior publication. RAM checks and inserts inside one transaction; the standalone SQLite path serializes its lookup and insert with an immediate transaction. Creation without that option is not automatically idempotent. Retention and direct-reminder claim transactions remain owned by Events; the browser adds neither a repository nor a scheduler.

HTTP and skill adapters

EventRoutes provides these notification endpoints independently of the scheduling feature gate:

Endpoint Behavior
GET /api/agent/notifications Optional normalized unread, read or dismissed filter; default limit 50, clamped to 1–500. Omit dismissed items unless requested or explicitly filtered. Return public records, whole-store counts and current enablement.
PATCH /api/agent/notifications/{notification_id} Set only read or dismissed; invalid or omitted status is rejected, and a missing record returns 404. Return the projected record and counts.
POST /api/agent/notifications/mark-all-read Mark all currently unread retained records read and return the changed count and totals. Leave dismissed records alone.

A GET does not acknowledge delivery. Status updates do not edit message content, stop an execution or change source lifecycle state. List records and totals are separate store reads, so a concurrent mutation can occur between them.

The Notification skill reuses these handlers plus ProductManagementService for create/get/dismiss. notification.delete means dismissal. Shared product-tool adapters retain the operation's declared read/write effect and normal authorization; registration does not itself grant permission or send email, chat messages or push.

Public payloads and privacy

notification_public.py starts with a detached model dump. It looks up linked event/task context and monitor context for known sensitive values and private macros. A nonempty task context takes precedence over the event context; monitor provenance is added separately. Title and message copies omit tagged think/analysis/reasoning blocks, strip controls and retain bounds of 160 and 24,000 characters. Ordinary credential projection follows the live Notifications redaction policy rather than changing execution or stored values.

Metadata permits only named scalar operational fields. Private context and arbitrary tool payloads are excluded; a conversation identity may be derived from the selected source context. Explicit error detail or a failed event/task/monitor invokes the mandatory public-error projection and its safe title/body/metadata processing. This is distinct from optional notification masking. Missing linked sources reduce available provenance; this function does not reconstruct deleted source history. See Redaction for policy ownership and limits.

Observing changes

update_stream.py publishes compact invalidations through the existing in-memory broker. Notification mutation wrappers publish notifications.changed after a successful store call; UI callbacks cannot undo committed storage. Reminder claims also observe notifications created inside their transaction and publish only after that claim returns successfully. These events tell a client to fetch current state; they are not notification bodies or durable delivery receipts. The broker's bounded cursor history can require a full refresh after a stale or restarted stream.

AsyncNotifications is the shared waiting primitive used by this broker and AgentTraceStore. Its name refers to observer wakeups, not inbox delivery. A reader registers an asyncio event, clears it and checks canonical readiness while holding the same lock as the writer. The writer schedules wakeups on each reader's loop. Readers recheck after wakeup, use one monotonic deadline and remove registrations on completion, timeout, cancellation or predicate failure. No polling thread or user notification is created.

The Notification Center tests exercise stored status, suppression, public provenance and producer content with local services. RAM event tests cover transaction rollback and source deduplication under contention; async observer tests check cross-thread wakeups and listener cleanup. The browser consumer lifecycle is described below.

Browser observation and alert ownership

notification_delivery.js is the shared, page-lived observer used by notification-enabled desktop surfaces. notifications_manager.js consumes its snapshots for Notification Center and independently reads upcoming reminders. Neither component creates notifications or determines whether the source operation succeeded.

flowchart TD Broker[Shared notifications and settings invalidations] --> Observer[Shared delivery observer] API[Canonical history, counts and enablement] --> Observer Observer --> Baseline[Known identities and creation watermark] Baseline --> Pending[Eligible new unread identities] Pending --> Delivery[Native or focused in-page delivery] Recent[Recent local identities and timestamps] --> Delivery Delivery --> Recent Recent <--> Tabs[Other tabs through storage and BroadcastChannel] Observer --> Center[Notification Center cards and unread badges] Center --> Actions[Explicit read, dismiss or mark-all-read action] Actions --> API Events[Saved direct-reminder definitions] --> Rail[Read-only Up next rail]

The initial successful history read establishes a silent delivery baseline. Later reads can alert only for an identity not already in the page's known set, with a creation time at or after the previous watermark, status: unread, and no explicit notifications_suppressed: true flag. Invalid creation dates cannot pass that comparison. Content edits, read/dismiss changes and loading older records do not create a new notification identity.

The page keeps at most 1,000 known identities in insertion order. Recent delivery identities are a separate map: local storage retains only IDs and timestamps, for up to seven days and at most 500 entries. These bounds concern browser observation and duplicate suppression, not server retention, unread counts or guaranteed exactly-once delivery.

History refresh and enablement sequence

sequenceDiagram participant B as Update broker or browser lifecycle participant O as Shared delivery observer participant A as Notification API participant C as Center and bell subscribers B->>O: Notification/settings change, focus or reconnect opt Settings changed or stream resync required O->>O: Gate alerts and hide current toast until refreshed end O->>O: Wait for shared read priority and coalesce reads O->>A: GET latest window including dismissed records alt Successful snapshot A-->>O: Records, whole-store counts and enablement alt First successful history load O->>O: Record baseline identities without arrivals else Later load O->>O: Queue eligible unknown IDs at or after prior watermark end alt Product alerts disabled O->>O: Clear pending alerts and current toast else Product alerts enabled O->>O: Drop missing, read, dismissed or suppressed pending IDs end O->>C: Publish current snapshot and capability status O->>O: Attempt eligible delivery else Read failure A-->>O: Error O->>C: Retain previous history and show refresh error Note over O,C: Error state blocks further alert draining end opt Another refresh arrived while the read was pending O->>A: Perform trailing read end

History starts at 100 items. Load more raises the read limit by 100 to a maximum of 500; every read includes dismissed records. One shared request coalesces callers, and another caller during the read requests a trailing pass. Idle invalidations use an 80 ms delay. Updates, focus, visibility recovery and the browser's online event cause refreshes; no interval polls the history endpoint.

Canonical enabled: false clears pending alerts and the active toast. A settings invalidation or stream resynchronization temporarily gates delivery until the next successful read establishes current enablement. Read failures preserve previously loaded history and expose a generic connection message. A later successful read clears the error and can deliver arrivals missed during that interruption.

Server unread totals drive badges even when the loaded or filtered history is smaller. Delivery, timeout, copy and preview expansion never PATCH read state. The explicit Enable browser notifications button is the only permission prompt: it calls the browser API only while permission is default. A secure context and native Notification support are required; browser permission does not override the product's alert setting.

Delivery selection and cross-tab coordination

flowchart TD Start[Pending alert drain] --> Gate{Ready to drain?} Gate -->|No| Hold[Keep current state until another trigger] Gate -->|Yes| Lock[Acquire optional Web Lock] Lock --> Recent[Merge recent IDs and drop delivered or ineligible items] Recent --> Native{Native delivery available?} Native -->|Yes| Attempt[Construct native notification with stable identity tag] Attempt -->|Construction succeeds| Remember[Remember identity and broadcast delivery metadata] Attempt -->|Construction fails| Latch[Latch native failure for this page] Latch --> Fallback[Consider in-page fallback] Remember --> Async{Later native error?} Async -->|Yes| Requeue[Remove local recent mark and requeue failed identity] Requeue --> Latch Async -->|No| Done[Native delivery remembered, inbox status unchanged] Native -->|No| Fallback Fallback --> Visible{Can show an in-page alert?} Visible -->|No| Hold Visible -->|Yes| Toast[Show one item, or summary after three individual alerts] Toast --> Saved[Remember displayed IDs without changing unread status] Saved --> Expiry[After 6.5 seconds, hide and drain next items] Expiry --> Start

A drain is ready only when alerts are enabled, refresh has no error and no other local drain is running. Native delivery requires granted permission and no latched native failure. In-page delivery requires pending items, no active toast, and a visible focused page.

A short optional Web Lock protects the cross-tab read/decide/remember step. If the browser lacks the API or rejects lock acquisition, delivery falls back to recent IDs, storage events, BroadcastChannel messages and stable native tags. An error after the lock callback has begun is propagated rather than rerunning the callback. There is no elected leader or heartbeat. Storage/channel restrictions reduce coordination to best effort; this is not a durable delivery protocol.

Native alerts use the current product display name, a plain-text body and the tag smto:{notification_id}. Clicking one focuses the existing window where allowed, navigates to its encoded Notification Center link, and closes the native alert. A constructor failure latches native fallback for this page. An asynchronous native error also requeues that identity after removing its local delivery mark. Other tabs can already have observed an earlier mark, so cross-tab behavior remains best effort rather than an exactly-once retry guarantee.

In-page alerts require a visible, focused page. They display one item at a time: three individual alerts per burst, then a summary for the remaining pending IDs. The summary links to the Center, while an individual alert links to its item. Hover or keyboard focus pauses the 6.5-second dismissal timer. Expiry advances the queue; the alert IDs are remembered when displayed, not when dismissed. Hiding the page removes its active toast without undoing that delivery mark or marking the inbox item read. Pending, undisplayed items wait for a later eligible drain.

The modules and their broker/browser listeners live for the document lifetime. pagehide clears the toast. They do not introduce a service worker, Web Push, background delivery after all pages close, or a second notification repository.

Center actions and bounded deep links

sequenceDiagram participant U as User or notification deep link participant C as Notification Center participant O as Shared delivery service participant A as Notification API opt URL selects a notification U->>C: Open encoded notification identity loop Missing from loaded window and more history is available below 500 C->>O: Load next 100 records O->>A: GET expanded window A-->>O: Canonical history O-->>C: Updated snapshot end alt Identity absent from recent history C-->>U: Explain that item is unavailable in recent history else Item retained opt Item is unread C->>C: Select read-status intent end end end opt Explicit card or bulk status action U->>C: Mark read, Dismiss or Mark all read C->>C: Select requested status mutation end opt A status mutation was selected C->>O: Guard duplicate local action and send intent O->>A: PATCH item or POST mark-all-read alt Write acknowledged O->>A: GET current history A-->>O: Snapshot or refresh failure O-->>C: Canonical data or retained data plus error else Write rejected O-->>C: Expose action error end C->>C: Reconcile cards and release local busy state end opt Deep-linked card remains visible under current filter C-->>U: Focus and briefly highlight card end

The Center searches only loaded title/message text, without regard to case, and sorts records newest first. Its selected status filter is retained in the UI session. Unchanged cards are reused; changed cards are rebuilt from literal headings, the shared Markdown renderer and public error presentation. Resize observation controls Show more when the preview overflows. Keyboard focus entering message links expands the preview. Removing/replacing cards releases their resize observations, and the view attempts to restore focus to the corresponding available action, card or filter.

Per-item busy state suppresses repeated card mutations. Failed writes remain visible on the card. A successful PATCH/POST followed by a failed refresh can leave the old snapshot on screen with a connection error; that read failure does not undo the acknowledged server mutation. Mark-all-read applies to retained unread records, not merely the loaded or visible subset.

A deep link is resolved once, with re-entry suppressed while history expands. Finding an unread record requests read status; dismissed records remain dismissed. Existing filters are not reset. For example, an Unread filter can hide the selected item after the read succeeds, so focus/highlight is conditional on its card remaining rendered. Use All and clear search to reveal a hidden item. A failed read-status write remains a card error and can be retried through its action.

Copy includes complete source title/message/public error text, even when the preview is collapsed. Clipboard API failure falls back to a temporary selected textarea, then restores the previously focused element. Copy failure reports feedback without changing notification status. Source links point to Schedules or an encoded conversation ID; notification content does not supply an arbitrary navigation URL.

Upcoming-reminder observation

sequenceDiagram participant B as Initial load or shared invalidation participant C as Notification Center reminder rail participant A as Event list endpoint participant S as Event store and scheduling settings B->>C: Open page, events/settings change or reconnect C->>C: Coalesce reads with an 80 ms invalidation delay C->>A: GET events with run_limit=1 A->>S: Read scheduling enablement alt Successful read alt Scheduling disabled A-->>C: Disabled result with empty event list else Scheduling enabled A->>S: Read saved definitions and run metadata A-->>C: Saved events and bounded recent run metadata end C->>C: Keep active scheduled direct reminders with valid next_run_at C->>C: Sort saved times and take first three C-->>B: Display labels and Schedules links else Read failure A-->>C: Error C->>C: Clear rail and expose Retry end

The rail reads /api/agent/events?run_limit=1. The event list handler returns an empty disabled result when scheduling is off. When enabled it reads saved event definitions, recent run summaries and open-run information. The browser uses only direct reminders with event_kind: scheduled, action_type: notification, status: active and a parseable saved next_run_at. It excludes conditional monitors, Agent schedules whose notification time depends on their outcome, and paused, cancelled or completed definitions.

The first three saved trigger times are formatted in each reminder's configured timezone; invalid timezone names fall back to UTC. The full timestamp/zone is available on the link. The rail does not recalculate recurrence, predict execution completion or fire a reminder. It uses a separate coalesced read with trailing refreshes, listens to event/settings changes and reconnect/visibility recovery, and shows explicit Retry after read failure. The notification history remains usable when the reminder read fails.

The browser fixtures exercise silent hydration, permission gestures, native/in-page fallback, suppression, cross-tab coordination, history mutations, deep links, retry, upcoming reminders and real local update-stream delivery. Native notifications are mocked; local stores and fake scheduling callbacks avoid live model/Gateway workloads. Appearance/theme acceptance is outside this review.
